targets.rationale: The model read the target and created no release event. The grader accurately describes that absence, but whether it constitutes a missed supported requirement is unresolved. August 7 is explicitly the release date and would support the keyed day if a release milestone belongs on Mark's calendar. The email does not request a calendar hold, assign Mark work, establish attendance, or identify an existing release object. The instructions explicitly allow no action for informational mail and caution against over-acting. An executive calendar milestone reading and an informational update reading are both defensible. Complete stores show no equivalent release milestone under a different title or email stamp, so this is not a demonstrated matching failure. There is also no evidence that the distinct August 10 launch commitments should move. A categorical MODEL attribution or categorical KEY defect would overstate the evidence.

evidence.observation: Observed get_email result says: "we need to delay the release of the new product to Friday, August 7th, 2026" and explains a design problem must be fixed before production. No personal task or calendar hold is stated.
"(no tool) — for FYIs, newsletters, confirmations, or anything needing no calendar/to-do change. Over-acting is the most common mistake; when in doubt, do nothing."

Inspected all events and todos in both stores. Only evt_17, Expo keynote on August 12, was added. No object represents the August 7 product release; all ten prior events and five prior todos remain unchanged.

The key requires create/event, match ["delayed"], exact_day August 7. The reported verdict is "FAIL — no event titled like "Delayed release date of new product" was created". The date is supported; obligatory event creation is the disputed inference.
The secretary MCP server is connected; successful target delivery and evt_17 creation rule out a demonstrated tool-disconnection explanation.

ambiguity_or_missing_evidence: No preceding storyline email establishes a tracked release milestone or earlier release date.
No supplied policy requires calendarizing every operational release announcement.
No supplied identity evidence connects this August 7 release to the August 10 public launch.
targets.suggested_human_question: Should a release-date announcement without a personal attendance or calendar request always create a milestone under this assistant policy?

sibling_observations.observation: The separate expo keynote has the correct August 12 day but an unsupported 10:00 start. Its email supplies no time, so the assistant instructions require 09:00 for one hour. This time/default issue does not determine T1's day-level verdict.
